AIA Art. 60(2) states that providers or prospective providers may conduct testing of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III in real world conditions at any time before the placing on the market or the putting into service of the AI system on their own or in partnership with one or more deployers or prospective deployers.

An AI system listed in Annex III is not considered high-risk if it performs a narrow procedural task, does not pose a significant risk of harm to the health, safety or fundamental rights of natural persons, and does not materially influence the outcome of decision-making.

If the provider considers that the AI system is not high-risk, they must document their assessment before placing the system on the market or putting it into service. They are also subject to the registration obligation set out in Article 49(2), which requires them to register themselves and the system in the EU database.

If the AI system is considered high-risk, the provider must follow the conformity assessment procedure outlined in Article 43. For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III, the provider must opt for a conformity assessment procedure based on either internal control or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation with the involvement of a notified body. For high-risk AI systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III, the provider must follow the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control without the involvement of a notified body.
